column2: Israel's collective offence and misappropriation precede Achar's named act; Carmi, Zambri and Zerah remain in the full selected genealogy.
Ai near Bethel is the destination, command and inspected city, retaining the repeated name.
About two or three thousand are recommended because the city's people are few; both prohibitions on bringing all the people remain.
About three thousand actually go and flee, distinguishing the executed number from the previous proposed range.
About thirty-six die, pursuit reaches the descent, and the people's terrified heart becomes like water.
Joshua and elders lie before the Lord until evening and put dust on their heads; tearing clothes remains Joshua's action.
Direct prayer uses Thee and Thy; Thy servant, not Thou, is the selected subject of bringing the people across, with the wish to have stayed beside Jordan retained.
Turning the neck is rendered idiomatically as turning the back before the enemy, preserving the retreat image.
Canaanites and all inhabitants surround and remove us; the final question concerns Thy great name without an invented answer.
The Lord commands rising and asks why Joshua has fallen like this, preserving the demonstrative force.
Sin, covenant transgression, theft from the ban and placement among belongings remain the explanation of defeat.
Inability to stand and retreat follow becoming subject to the ban; divine presence is withheld unless the banned thing is removed.
Joshua consecrates the people for tomorrow and relays the Lord's declaration that the ban is among them until removed.
Selection narrows through tribes, clans, households and individual men, with divine indication repeated at each level.
Burning the indicated person and everything belonging to him is tied to covenant transgression and lawlessness, without softening the stated sanction.
Joshua rises early and Judah is indicated after the tribal approach.
The Zerahite clan is indicated and approach proceeds man by man in this shorter selected account.
Achar is son of Zambri, son of Zerah here; Carmi from 7:1 is not inserted into the shorter genealogy.
Glory today, confession, reporting and not concealing form the four-part appeal to Achar.
The confession names the Lord God of Israel and introduces the specifics; this is what I did represents the houtos kai houtos idiom.
Restore Behold before the hidden goods for explicit idou. The patterned carpet, two hundred silver didrachms and one fifty-didrachm gold tongue remain distinct.
column3: Psile as carpet and the tongue-shaped bar interpretation are provisional lexical choices; no new specialist textile or metrological consultation is claimed.

column2: Messengers run to the camp tent and find the goods with silver beneath, confirming the confession's placement.
The goods go to Joshua and elders and are placed before the Lord, retaining all recipients and the final location.
Propose calves for moschous rather than generic cattle. The shorter Achar son of Zerah, both Achor and Emek-achor, family, other animals, tent and possessions all remain.
Joshua addresses Achar, and the selected object of stoning is singular him; the sentence is not expanded to assert the fate of every accompanying person.
The stone heap is over him, divine wrath ceases, and Emek-achor remains the named place to this day.
Fear and faintheartedness are prohibited before all fighting men rise to Ai; the king and land are already declared delivered into Joshua's hands.
Ai is compared with Jericho, but livestock spoil is authorized; the ambush is behind the city.
Joshua and the fighting people rise; he chooses thirty thousand mighty men and sends them at night.
The ambush stays behind the city without being far away, with all to remain ready.
Joshua's group approaches and feigns the earlier flight when Ai's inhabitants come out.
The pursuit draws inhabitants from the city, and their expected report explicitly compares the flight with before.
The ambush group then rises and enters the city; no unexpressed delivery promise is appended to this short unit.
The selected short command retains according to this word and behold, without an added burning instruction here.
The ambush lies between Bethel and Ai, west of Ai, preserving the sea-side directional idiom.
Joshua inspects the people at morning, then he and the elders go ahead toward Ai.
The fighting people approach opposite the city from the east, not a substituted northern approach.
The ambush is west; the selected shorter statement and following 8:13 numbering gap remain.
The king hastens straight into battle with his people, unaware of the ambush behind the city.
Joshua sees and withdraws, with Israel also withdrawing; no unexpressed defeat is asserted here.
The pursuers follow Israel and draw away from the city, fulfilling the plan.
Nobody remains who does not pursue; the repeated pursuit accompanies the city's open condition.
The hand with the javelin is extended toward the city, and the ambush is promised a quick rising; both command and fulfilment remain.
column3: With the javelin supplies the English relation of the difficult accusative hand/javelin construction in the fulfilment clause; this remains a syntactic question, not a new textual reading.

column2: The ambush rises at the extended hand, captures the city and hastens to burn it, retaining the repeated speed expressions.
Looking back reveals smoke to heaven, and no escape this way or that remains.
Joshua and Israel see both capture and smoke, turn and strike Ai's men.
The city force emerges and the enemy is caught between both groups; survivor and fugitive remain separate exclusions.
column3: The source's repeated demonstratives require contextual assignment of opposing groups; inherited others and they are provisional referent resolutions.

column2: The king alone is explicitly captured alive and brought to Joshua.
Plains, mountain and descent remain in the pursuit description before Joshua returns to strike the city.
column3: The attachment of on the descent, from it and to the end in the terrain clause is difficult; inherited wording preserves the elements without claiming resolved topography.

column2: Twelve thousand men and women fall, identified as all Ai's inhabitants, before the spoil exception in 8:27.
Livestock and city spoil are excepted and taken under the Lord's command; the 8:26 gap remains without an invented verse.
Joshua burns the city and makes a perpetually uninhabited mound, with to this day retained alongside for ever.
The king hangs on a forked tree until evening; sunset removal, the pit and a stone heap remain, without substituting a gate location.
column3: Didymon literally describes a doubled form; forked tree is provisional and does not settle the object's construction.

column2: The geographic list includes Anti-Lebanon and the people list repeats Amorites after their initial kings, with Girgashites retained.
All the kings assemble together against Joshua and Israel before the selected inserted Ebal sequence.
Joshua builds on Ebal here at 9:2a, preserving the Greek placement rather than relocating the episode to chapter 8.
Whole stones untouched by iron, whole burnt offerings and a soteriou sacrifice remain. Propose sacrifice of deliverance for well-being to match the working rendering of this selected ritual phrase.
column3: Deliverance is a source-led working term, not a claim that the technical sacrificial category has received complete specialist review.

column2: The second law, Moses' law, is written on the stones before Israel, preserving deuteronomion rather than silently choosing copy.
column3: The second-law/copy-law sense and the subject of the final wrote clause require further review.

column2: All Israel and officials stand in relation to the ark, with priests and Levites carrying it; alien/native and Gerizim/Ebal halves remain.
column3: The placement of first with Moses' command or the blessing action remains a syntactic question.

column2: Joshua reads all law, blessings and curses according to everything written, retaining the totalizing repetition.
No commanded word is omitted for men, women, children and travelling resident aliens, preserving the double-negative completeness statement.
The Lord, not Joshua, is the selected agent whose deeds at Jericho and Ai the Gibeonites hear.
Their craft involves provisioning, preparation, old donkey sacks and old torn tied wineskins, with the separate actions retained.
Footwear soles, old patched sandals, worn clothes and bread dry, mouldy and eaten away all remain in the deception's material details.
column3: Koila of footwear and the exact repair sense of katapepelmatomena remain technical lexical questions.

column2: They approach Joshua and Israel at Gilgal, claim a distant origin and request a covenant.
The selected Horite and Israel's collective singular my/I remain, without harmonizing the ethnic designation or grammatical number.
Propose household servants for oiketai, distinct from paides at 9:9; Joshua's two origin questions remain.
Servants remains for paides, with very distant origin, divine name and the Egypt report retained; no global servant replacement is made.
Sihon of Heshbon and Og of Bashan are named, with Og dwelling in both Ashtaroth and Edrei.
Propose household servants for the repeated oiketai self-description. Elders and all inhabitants commission the journey, provisions and covenant request.
The bread was allegedly hot on departure and is now dry and eaten away, preserving the temporal contrast.
Newly filled skins are now torn and clothes and sandals worn from the exceedingly long journey claimed.
The leaders take provisions but do not inquire of the Lord; the selected leaders, rather than an unspecified men, are retained.
Joshua makes peace and a covenant to preserve them, and the congregation's leaders swear, retaining the different agents.
Three days after the covenant they learn the people are nearby and resident among them.
The four cities remain Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth and the city of Jearim in order.
No fighting follows because all leaders swore by the Lord God of Israel, while the whole congregation grumbles.
The leaders repeat the oath as the reason they cannot touch the Gibeonites.
Keeping alive and preserving avert wrath because of the oath, retaining both protective verbs.
Life is joined to woodcutting and water carrying for the whole congregation, as the leaders stated.
Joshua says deceived me but dwelling among us, preserving the individual accusation and collective residence.
A slave and woodcutter will never be lacking for me and my God; no absent water-carrier or house-of-God phrase is imported here.
The Gibeonites report the divine order to give the land and destroy us and all inhabitants, with fear for their lives as their motive.
They yield themselves under plural your power and judgment; ordinary English you does not make this exclusively singular address to Joshua.
They did so is plural before Joshua's singular rescue, followed by the Israelites not killing them.
Woodcutters and water-carriers are assigned to congregation and God's altar, then repeated for Gibeon's inhabitants through the present and the chosen place.
